# TSFMC
The [color=cyan]Trans-Solarian Federation Marine Corps[/color] detachment is one of the primary actors in the Colossus Sector. These marines, supposedly here to "keep the peace", are heavily-armed and wield advanced weapons technology. Their domination is only hindered by the threats posed by the [color=purple]Monolith's[/color] anomalies. While powerful, the main forces of the TSFMC are seperated, blockaded by the [color=purple]interference[/color] around the Colossus sector, and are thus liable to being picked off by opponents. As such, TSFMC marines, despite their futuristic gadgets, have been forced into a defensive position. Their gear reflects this, with heavier weapons and durable equipment.
In-sector, they are primarily in conflict with the resident [color=orange]Phaethon Dynasty[/color], a local developing empire much more used to the anomalies and action of the Colossus sector, though during each emission period they may make more enemies.
Their objectives in the sector, as briefed by their High Command before dropping into the Monolith radius, are to:
- Confiscate and study Corporate-war era technology
- Eliminate opposition and establish control over the sector
After dropping in, however, the actual task marines face is clear: Survival. To meet this goal, federation military personnel follow the orders of their higher officers, which usually involves collecting resources from debris and detritus to strengthen their local military, fending off anomalous threats, and studying any relevant technology. While this might not be what High Command has in mind, they aren't exactly able to reach you or know what you are doing in-sector - and neither are the outer sectors. Remember, the Colossus sector is a bloody place, and no doubt will some of that be shed by your hand.
# Personnel and Ranking
[color=cyan]The TSF Marine Corps division[/color]'s staff is made up, in order of authority, by [color=gold]Colonels[/color], [color=silver]Captains[/color], [color=cyan]Fireteam Leaders[/color], [color=orange]Marines[/color] (of multiple roles), and [color=gray]Cyborgs[/color].
[color=gold]Colonels[/color] =============================== Each fleet operation of the TSF is headed by a [color=gold]Colonel[/color], a high-ranking and (usually) experienced officer of the Federation. While they may head operations themselves, commanding a vessel and soaring into the fray, colonels who do so often don't return and become a detriment to the operation as a whole. When playing as a [color=gold]Colonel[/color], remember that you are the authority in this sector, at the very least for your marines. Despite this, keep in mind the realities your troops fight against - A bad colonel is an ignored colonel.
[color=gold]Colonels[/color] answer only to themselves and to [color=cyan]TSF High Command[/color]. They have the highest authority in the local sector's combat operations.
[color=silver]Captains[/color] =============================== Each main battlecarrier of the TSF is helmed and commanded by a [color=silver]Captain[/color], an experienced officer familiar with the operation of their vessel and usually dependable in combat. While they often stay onboard in safety, they are nonetheless familiar with conflict and managing lower ranking marines - Even with significant firepower and hull between them and the enemy, crewing a battlecarrier is a dangerous task.
[color=silver]Captains[/color] answer to [color=gold]Colonels[/color] and have jurisdiction over their vessel.
[color=cyan]Fireteam Leaders[/color] (FTLs) =============================== [color=cyan]Fireteam Leaders[/color] command ground forces and function as squad leaders, organizing their marine platoon during ground- and small-scale space-combat. They are a marine's closest connection to fleet command, and as such FTLs should communicate with their platoons consistently and frequently. Organization wins wars.
[color=cyan]Fireteam Leaders[/color] answer to [color=silver]Captains[/color] and command their own platoon, assigned to them by themselves or by one of their superiors.
[color=orange]Marines[/color] =============================== Marines fall into multiple roles: and [color=orange]Marines[/color], [color=red]Corpsmen[/color] and [color=yellow]Engineers[/color], each with their own tasks but sharing command authority.
[color=orange]Marines[/color] are the lowest ranking members of the TSFMC, operating their fighters under the command of a Fireteam Leader. They conduct boarding operations, extract technology, and generally do the grunt combat work.
[color=red]Corpsmen[/color] are critical to a successful operation, acting as medical professionals in times of combat. If a marine is shredded, a Corpsman is the one to keep them alive. Their goal is to preserve the lives of other TSF members, but they aren't afraid to shoot some rounds themselves.
[color=yellow]Engineers[/color] are like corpsmen to the TSF navy. If a ship has half its hull gone from a railgun shot, Engineers are the ones to make it seem like the ship came right from the drydock. They prioritize repairs and modifications to existing ships, handle logistics, and create fortifications.
[color=orange]Marines[/color] answer to every high ranking officer.
